lessons.title: Il y a: what exists
lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Hay: what exists: Hay means there is or there are.
lessons.objective: Say what exists with il y a and where something is with être; negate existence with il n’y a pas de or d’ before a vowel.
lessons.focus: Il y a means there is or there are and does not change for number. Use est, a form of être, for where a particular thing is. In il n’y a pas de + noun, de replaces un, une or des; write d’ before a vowel: il n’y a pas d’ordinateur. Review la/une/les with noun gender and number.
lessons.scene: Léa is new to the school. Théo shows her the library and the nearby study area.
dialogue: Léa : Il y a une bibliothèque ici ?|Is there a library here?
Théo : Oui, elle est là, près de la cantine.|Yes, it is there, near the cafeteria.
Léa : Il y a des tables ?|Are there tables?
Théo : Oui, il y a des tables et deux fenêtres.|Yes, there are tables and two windows.
Léa : Et il y a des livres sur la table ?|And are there books on the table?
Théo : Oui, il y a des livres sur la table. La table est près de la porte.|Yes, there are books on the table. The table is near the door.
Léa : Il n’y a pas d’ordinateur ici, c’est ça ?|There is no computer here, right?
Théo : Non, il n’y a pas d’ordinateur ici.|No, there is no computer here.
lessons.speaking: Role-play a new student asking a classmate about the school library; use tu. Open with Salut ! Ask Il y a une bibliothèque ici ? Name two things present with il y a, then locate one with est près de or est sur. Ask whether there is a computer; answer with il n’y a pas d’ordinateur. Confirm one detail with C’est ça ? and close with Merci ! Your partner explains an unfamiliar word in English when asked.

lessons.title: Numbers and age
lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Numbers and age: Use tener for age: tengo dieciocho años, literally I have eighteen years.
lessons.objective: Give an assigned age with avoir (j’ai dix-huit ans), count 1–20, and say how many students there are and how many books a class needs.
lessons.focus: French uses avoir for age: j’ai dix-huit ans, literally “I have eighteen years,” never je suis. Learn j’ai, tu as, il/elle a, nous avons; Tu as quel âge ? asks “How old are you?” Use il y a for a count and avoir besoin de + number + noun for a need. Count 1–20, including dix-huit and vingt. Pronunciation: dix is /dis/ alone, /di/ before a consonant, /diz/ before a vowel; dix-huit is /dizɥit/ and vingt ans links the final t. There is no elision before onze: de onze livres.
lessons.scene: The class group list. Inès and Sami, two classmates, fill in the group sheet with ages, books, and the class number.
dialogue: Inès : Bonjour ! Tu as quel âge ?|Hello! How old are you?
Sami : J’ai dix-huit ans. Et toi ?|I am eighteen years old. And you?
Inès : J’ai dix-huit ans aussi ! Mon frère a vingt ans.|I am eighteen too! My brother is twenty years old.
Sami : Il y a dix élèves dans la classe, c’est ça ?|There are ten students in the class, right?
Inès : Oui. Nous avons besoin de dix livres pour les élèves et d’un livre pour la professeure.|Yes. We need ten books for the students and one book for the teacher.
Sami : Donc, onze livres. Moi, j’ai un livre et deux cahiers.|So, eleven books. I have one book and two notebooks.
Inès : C’est la salle quinze ?|Is this room fifteen?
Sami : Oui, c’est ça. Parfait !|Yes, that’s right. Perfect!
lessons.speaking: Role-play filling a class list with another student; use tu. Open with Salut ! Tu as quel âge ? For practice, use an assigned age of dix-huit or vingt ans; ask your partner the same. State that there are dix élèves and that the group needs dix livres plus one for the teacher. Confirm the total onze livres and room quinze. Close with Merci, à demain ! Do not use être for age. Your partner explains unfamiliar words in English when asked.
